description.en-US: The return's own reference, allocated on create and never reused. Separate from the order number because a return is its own document (BR 59): a partial return never rewrites the order it came from, so the two need distinct identities for anyone reconciling them later.
The order whose goods are coming back. Immutable: a return that could be re-pointed at a different order would move money and stock between two unrelated sales.

Where the return has reached COMMERCIALLY. Per D-17 it reaches 'completed' once the goods are back and the money is refunded — the customer-facing halves — and NOT when the tax paperwork succeeds. fiscal_adjustment_status carries that separately and never gates this one. Moved only by the return service, never by a plain update.

Whether the goods have physically come back. 'not_required' is the ordinary state for a return of services or non-stocked lines, which complete on the refund alone (D-32). One of the two halves that decide 'completed'.
Whether the customer has been paid back. 'not_required' covers a return against an order that was never paid — there is nothing to give back. The other half that decides 'completed'.

Whether the VAT invoice has been corrected with the authority. INDEPENDENT of status by design (BR 66, D-17): a failure here must never roll back goods already returned or money already refunded, and must never take money back from a customer. A 'failed' value is a retryable to-do for Accounting, not a customer-facing problem, and retrying it does not move the return's own status.
Why the goods are coming back. Mandatory: a return moves money out of the business, and one with no stated reason cannot be audited or disputed later.

What should happen to the goods once back — business intent only. Inventory decides the actual location and movement (BR 56); naming a warehouse here would put Inventory's decisions in Sales, which is the separation BR 44 exists to keep.

What the customer is owed, computed from the HISTORICAL amounts the returned quantities actually carried (BR 60), never from a current price. Includes any promotion clawback, capped so a clawback larger than the refund never turns the refund negative (D-12).
Inventory's own handle for the incoming movement, once it has accepted one. The only durable link to what physically happened, so it is stored rather than re-derived.
Why the most recent step failed, in the words of whichever system refused it. Kept so an operator retrying has something to act on rather than a bare 'failed'.

When the return was raised. Stored rather than read from created_at because the return window is measured against the ORDER, and having both timestamps side by side is what makes that check auditable.
When the return became commercially complete — goods back and money refunded. Deliberately unrelated to when the tax correction succeeded, which may be later or never.
When the return was called off, which is only possible before anything irreversible has happened.
